FINAL NATURAL-LANGUAGE HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, ready for submission):

"Considering academic characteristics does not merely shrink the effects of family Socioeconomic Status (SES) and race on BA-degree attainment in the NLSY79 sample (nls_raw.csv, N=12,686) — it reframes them. Because this dataset contains no direct BA-completion variable (respondent education is recorded only by 'Highest grade completed, 1979', which is age-censored in 1979), BA completion is proxied (grade >= 16) and statistically underpowered; the primary evidence therefore concerns college entry by 1979 (grade >= 13) and total years of schooling by 1979 among respondents aged 19+. Descriptively, Black ('Racial/ethnic cohort, 1979'=1) and Hispanic (=2) respondents are less likely than Non-Black/Non-Hispanic (=3) respondents to have entered college (21.3% and 22.0% vs 28.7%) and have ~0.8 and ~0.4 fewer years of completed schooling, mirroring their lower family income ('Total net family income, previous calendar year, 1979'), lower parental education ('Highest grade completed by respondent's mother/father, 1979'), and far lower ASVAB subscores (composite ~420–440 vs ~515). Controlling for family SES (log income + mean parental education) eliminates the raw minority disadvantage in years of schooling (−0.84→−0.03 Black; −0.36→−0.02 Hispanic; both non-significant), showing the raw race gap is almost entirely SES-driven, with parental education as the dominant channel. Controlling additionally for academic characteristics — the four 1981 ASVAB subscores ('ASVAB - Arithmetic Reasoning / Word Knowledge / Paragraph Comprehension / Mathematics Knowledge Z Score (rounded), 1981', composited and standardized) — REVERSES the race effects to significantly positive: conditional on family background and measured ability, Hispanic respondents complete +0.63 more years of schooling (p<1e-9) and Black respondents +0.21 (p=0.08) than comparable White respondents, with college-entry average marginal effects of +18.5pp (Black) and +23.6pp (Hispanic) versus +22.7pp per SD of ASVAB. This is a suppression pattern, not attenuation: minority respondents average much lower ASVAB and SES, so the raw disadvantage masks composition; holding background and ability constant, minority attainment is comparable-or-higher than Whites'. The sign-flip is robust to adding family net wealth ('Family net wealth, 1985') and father's occupation ('Occupation of adult male in household at age 14, 1979') as extra SES controls, and to multiple-imputation sensitivity for the Hispanic advantage (+0.61 yrs, SE 0.01) though the Black advantage shrinks to ~0 (+0.01, SE 0.006) in the less-selected imputed sample. Mediation shows SES operates substantially through academic ability: parental education's indirect effect via ASVAB is +0.10 years (Sobel p<1e-14) and log family income's +0.02 (p=0.018), with SES coefficients shrinking ~38–48% once ASVAB enters; minority status INDIRECTLY lowers attainment through the ASVAB pathway (−0.24 Black, −0.65 Hispanic years, Sobel z<−6), which is the composition-driven component of the raw gap. A moderation check is ancillary: the ASVAB-to-attainment slope is significantly larger for Black respondents (interaction +0.46 yrs/SD, p=5.9e-5) but not Hispanic (ns). BA completion itself can only be proxied by 'Highest grade completed, 1979' >= 16 among respondents aged 21+ — only 34 events (1.61%): raw rates Black 1.05%, Hispanic 0.86%, White 1.98%, with the same direction-reversal in an underpowered illustrative logit (Black +0.67, Hispanic +1.32, ASVAB +1.47). Overall: SES affects attainment largely THROUGH academic characteristics, and net of SES and academic ability the minority-vs-White gaps in college entry/attainment reverse from a disadvantage to comparable-or-higher minority attainment — so accounting for academic characteristics alters the estimated effects of both SES (attenuated, partially mediated) and race (sign-reversed via suppression)."

FULL DIAGNOSTICS, MODEL TABLES, AND MISSINGNESS ARE IN analysis_results.txt (and summarized in evidence below).

payload.workflow: NLSY79 (nls_raw.csv): missingness table; age-gated (age>=19) complete-case analysis on two outcomes (any college entry = Highest grade completed,1979 >=13, and continuous Highest grade completed,1979 years) with logit/OLS model sequences race+demographics -> +SES (log income-1979, mean parental education) -> +ASVAB composite (4 subscores, standardized); robustness adding family net wealth 1985 and father's 1979 occupation; race x ASVAB moderation; product-of-coefficients/Sobel mediation via ASVAB; BA proxy (grade>=16, age>=21) descriptive + flagged illustrative logit; MICE-lite imputation sensitivity. Framing descriptive/associational, no causal claims.
